purpose: Frozen, truthful record of the pre-repair (broken-instrument) pipeline.

environment.note: The Bash-tool default 'python' is Python 3.14 WITHOUT torch. All torch code must use the Anaconda interpreter above.

reproducibility.evidence: The registry run (exp_20260522_021449) and the checkpoint re-run logged metrics that are bit-identical to full float precision (best_val_f1=0.3176470588235294, final_val_roc_auc=0.9275197982788086, final_rca_accuracy=0.53125). Training is deterministic under seed=42; the apparent RCA discrepancy (0.50 vs 0.53125) is best-epoch vs final-epoch reporting of the SAME run, not run-to-run variance.

key_observations: val_roc_auc is stable at 0.92-0.95 across all 30 epochs (peak epoch 3 = 0.9544). The model's ranking ability is good and stable.
val_f1 is low and noisy (0.04-0.32). rca_accuracy is pure noise (0.28-0.625). The reported failure is in the instruments, not the model.
F5 confirmed: early-stopping on val_f1 picked epoch 27 (AUC 0.9350); AUC was HIGHER at epoch 3 (0.9544). The stopping signal selects a worse model by the trustworthy metric.

artifacts_to_repair.F1: compute_rca_accuracy fed per-batch tensors (validate() lines 563-565); a 4-graph batch scored as one graph.
artifacts_to_repair.F2: F1 read at hard-coded 0.5 threshold (compute_metrics line 377) under pos_weight up to 1665.
artifacts_to_repair.F3: 3 of 6 loss terms (cpu/gpu/job) are all-negative and trivial; dilute gradient budget ~50%.
artifacts_to_repair.F4: batch_size=4 + pos_weight=332 -> sparse, high-variance positive gradients.
artifacts_to_repair.F5: early-stopping tracks val_f1, the corrupted metric.

validation_criteria.baseline_checkpoint_frozen: PASS - checkpoints/baseline_model.pt is a byte copy, never to be overwritten.
